alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).

Cohortative rendered by light verb + complement 'take heed', headed on heed (rule 44); the supplied 'to' reaches the verb's bare object דְרָכַי and joins the verb's unit (rule 44 supplied-preposition clause).

Privative מִן + infinitive recast as negative clause: complementizer 'That' and negation 'not' both belong to the preposition (rule 48); headed on 'not' as the word carrying the privative force, 'That' being the competing head.
Infinitive takes its supplied subject pronoun (rule 48).

Cohortative with subject and auxiliary. מַחְסוֹם is this verb's direct object in the Hebrew ('keep a muzzle for my mouth'); the ASV keeps the verb a verb, promotes 'my mouth' to its object and demotes the Hebrew object to an instrument, so the supplied 'with' is the verb's under rule 33's direct-object paragraph (PRO.7.16 'I have spread my couch with carpets') and rule 44; discontinuous around 'my mouth' (rule 25). Competing reading: 'with' on the noun as a supplied function word under rule 33's first sentence.
The לְ of 'for my mouth' is silenced: ASV promotes mouth to the direct object of keep (rule 40).

Hebrew direct object rendered 'a bridle'; the supplied indefinite article joins the noun (rule 15), while the 'with' the recasting supplies belongs to the verb (rule 33 direct-object paragraph). Margin gloss read and set aside (rule 38).

בְּעוֹד rendered by the single word 'While'; fused under rule 30, headed on עוֹד as the morpheme carrying the temporal content, as בְּטֶרֶם → Before is in verse 13. Competing reading: 'While' on the בְּ under rule 52 with עוֹד unrepresented.
לְנֶגֶד rendered by one word 'before' (rule 30 fusion, headed on נֶגֶד); the prepositional predicate takes the construction's copula 'is' (rule 49).

review_notes: Reconciliation: 'with' of 'with a bridle' moved from מַחְסוֹם to אֶשְׁמְרָה (rule 33 direct-object paragraph; PRO.7.16 shape). Privative מִן split per rule 48; בְּעוֹד fused per rule 30.
